introduction: Ohio WIC supplies nutrition support for eligible pregnant, postpartum and breastfeeding participants, infants and children younger than five. Enrollment happens through a local clinic.
description: Ohio WIC supplies nutrition support for eligible pregnant, postpartum and breastfeeding participants, infants and children younger than five. Enrollment happens through a local cli

sections.who: The clinic checks residence, income and nutritional risk. Columbus Public Health lists the Ohio income guideline as 185% of federal poverty guidelines.
sections.get: Services include selected nutritious foods, nutrition counseling, breastfeeding support and referrals. WIC is separate from SNAP.
sections.docs:
• Identification, birth-date and address evidence.
  • Income records and any Medicaid or SNAP information.
  • Pregnancy documentation when requested; bring participating children as instructed.
sections.apply:
1. Find a clinic

    Contact the WIC clinic serving your county. Franklin County residents can use Columbus Public Health WIC or call 614-645-7280.

  2. Arrange certification

    Ask what to bring and who must attend.

  3. Complete assessment

    The clinic reviews eligibility and explains food benefits and follow-up visits.
sections.after: Use benefits within their assigned period and keep clinic appointments. Confirm local procedures rather than assuming statewide walk-in intake.
sections.sources: Content checked October 1, 2026 using Columbus WIC services and certification. Current eligibility and the final decision remain with the program.

faqs: Is the Columbus phone statewide intake?
No. It serves Franklin County; use your local clinic elsewhere.
Does WIC cover every grocery item?
No. Benefits cover the assigned food package.
Can SNAP recipients ask about WIC?
Yes. Bring benefit information for the clinic to review.
Call the clinic first; Columbus currently requires appointments.
